description: I'm Abdullahi, a 400-level Electrical Engineering student at LAUTECH, Nigeria. I build embedded AI and IoT systems, including SAOT (agri IoT) and SP3 (solar cold storage for farmers). FloodSense is a gamified platform using NASA data to teach Terai farmers to read flood risk. Join for a clear plan, defined roles and a playable demo. We need a UI/UX designer, a GIS/remote sensing person, a storyteller for the pitch, and anyone who knows South Asian agriculture.
summary:
Every monsoon, floods catch farmers in Nepal's Terai off guard, even though the warning signs build for days. Rain piles up, the soil fills, and rivers rise upstream. Satellites see all of it, but farmers rarely get it in a form they can use. FloodSense is our answer: a mobile app for farmers in Jhapa, available in Nepali, Rajbanshi and English. It turns NASA rainfall (GPM IMERG), soil moisture (SMAP), land cover (MODIS) and atmospheric (MERRA-2) data into something farmers can read and act on. They can explore a risk map, get a simple farm checklist for their crop, and play through real past monsoon seasons, judging the risk before seeing what happened and why. For the Earth System Trend Detective challenge, we analyse these NASA time series with the Mann-Kendall test to show whether changes in rainfall and soil moisture are statistically significant, and whether the current season is unusual compared with history.

The goal is to help farmers spot danger early enough to protect their crops, stored produce and livelihoods. FloodSense is learning and decision support, not an official warning.
details:
FloodSense is a mobile web app that teaches farmers in Jhapa, in Nepal’s Terai, to read flood warning signs. It turns NASA data (GPM IMERG rainfall, SMAP soil moisture, MODIS land cover, MERRA-2, plus SRTM elevation) into a risk map with plain-word reasons, a “My Farm” checklist matched to the farmer’s crop and growth stage, and a game where farmers replay real past monsoon weeks and see what happened and why. A trends view tests seasonal changes with the Mann-Kendall test and flags unusual seasons. We built it with Python for the analysis and an explainable ML model, and Vite, React, TypeScript, Tailwind, Leaflet and Recharts for the app, hosted on Vercel, with no special hardware. It is creative because it teaches the reasoning behind flood risk instead of just showing a rainfall map. We designed for local needs with Nepali, Rajbanshi and English, icons, and a very simple first round. We were honest about the limits: the data is coarse, flooding depends on upstream conditions, and the app is decision support, not an official warning. The aim is for farmers to spot danger early enough to protect their crops, stored produce and livelihoods.

  • What it does: a risk map, a crop-specific “My Farm” checklist, and a game replaying real past monsoon weeks, plus a trends view with Mann-Kendall significance testing.
  • Benefits: farmers learn how rain, soil saturation and upstream conditions combine to cause floods, so they can act earlier on harvesting and storage.
  • Impact: a shift from reacting to floods to recognising danger early, protecting crops, stored produce and livelihoods.
  • Tools: NASA GPM IMERG, SMAP, MODIS, MERRA-2 and SRTM; Python and an explainable ML model; Vite, React, TypeScript, Tailwind, Leaflet, Recharts; Vercel. No special hardware.
  • Creativity: it teaches why a field is vulnerable, using gamified replays of real seasons with farm decisions and consequences.
  • Factors considered: local languages and literacy, coarse data limits, upstream flooding, honest “not an official warning” framing, expert review of guidance and translations, and a mobile-friendly build with fallbacks.
